summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency constraints and compliance controls for Riverdale Bank. Bank is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for LLM inference. Key concerns: EU/UK data residency, customer-managed keys, limited logging/audit retention for sensitive workloads, SOC2/PCI/HIPAA coverage. Next steps are to share security artifacts, schedule infra deep-dive and produce pricing for dedicated/private options.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-30 15:00 ET
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Riverdale Head of Data), Carlos Ramirez (Riverdale Lead Cloud Engineer), Sophie Lin (Riverdale Legal/Compliance), Ethan Park (Product Manager)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me are Priya and Daniel on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. We wanted to do a discovery call - mainly around where we can host inference and what controls exist for regulated data.
[00:15] Alex: Great, that's what we'll cover - quickly run through Riverdale's use cases and constraints, then Priya will talk architecture options (hosted, dedicated, private) and Daniel can cover logging/audit and KMS.
[00:27] Ethan: Cool. For context: we want to ship a conversational assistant and some back-office automation that will touch customer PII and some PCI-adjacent info. We also have EU/UK customers so residency matters.
[00:38] Priya: Understood. Quick question - which regs are you most worried about? Is it PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, local banking regs, or a combination?
[00:45] Sophie: It's a combination. GDPR residency + data subject rights are top for EU flows. For US, PCI for card workflows and we have some healthcare-related notes so HIPAA is a maybe depending on scope. Also internal audit expects key separation and ability to show non-repudiable audit logs.
[00:59] Carlos: And from infra: we can't allow raw logs with full customer PII to be stored in a third-party S3 without controls and we prefer customer-managed keys for any persistent storage.
[01:12] Alex: That's fair. At a high level, Redwood hosted can serve EU-region endpoints (we have infra in eu-west-1 and europe-west-2) and we support per-customer data tagging and retention policies, but there are limits around log redaction and KMS access in hosted. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more control over network egress, and Private gives the most isolation - private control plane and option for customer-managed KMS/HSM on-prem.
[01:38] Maya: When you say "option for customer-managed KMS", does that mean Redwood can use our KMS keys in our account?
[01:44] Priya: Yes - for Private we can integrate with customer KMS via a key-wrapping or external key store pattern; for Dedicated we can provide KMS integration in a supported setup but often keys are managed in a Redwood-managed account with CMKs that we rotate. Hosted typically uses Redwood-managed keys.
[02:01] Sophie: That's a blocker for some of our regulated workloads - we need proof that keys are customer-controlled and that key use is logged in our audit trails. Also we need a mechanism to revoke access quickly.
[02:13] Daniel: We can show a key rotation and access log sample from our Private deployments; we also integrate with HSM-backed KMS if you require FIPS-level protection. One note - Private requires networking work (VPC peering or private link) and some on-prem firewall rules.
[02:28] Carlos: Ok, how about logs - specifically request/response logs. Our policy is not to persist full request bodies containing PII beyond X hours and to have redaction available. What does Redwood persist?
[02:40] Priya: By default we persist minimal telemetry for 30 days for debugging, rate limiting and billing. For Hosted we keep a transcript-like trace for a short period but we do not store prompt/response payloads long-term unless you opt-in. For Dedicated you can configure retention and choose to disable request logging; Private gives you total control - logs can be shipped to your central logging with redact/transform pipelines.
[03:05] Maya: What's the granularity of redaction? Can you redact entities via regex or a PII detector?
[03:11] Priya: We support both. We have a PII detector module that can pre-process and mask tokens server-side; we can also apply regex redaction at ingestion. For critical flows we usually recommend edge-side redaction before sending to the model so nothing sensitive leaves your network.
[03:26] Ethan: If we do edge redaction, will that affect model quality for customer-facing responses?
[03:31] Daniel: Potentially - depends on the info removed. For many intents, masked tokens are fine; for personalized responses you may want a tokenization strategy or use pseudonymization so the model maintains context without exposing raw PII.
[03:46] Sophie: Back to compliance - do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs? And can you provide artifact evidence for audit?
[03:53] Alex: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001; I'll share the certs and a security whitepaper. We can also provide architecture diagrams for Private deployments and an attestation for access controls.
[04:05] Carlos: For EU residency, do you do data processing agreements and EU SCCs?
[04:11] Alex: We have standard DPA and we support SCCs where needed, and we can localize processing to EU regions for EU customers. For Private deployments if you deploy into your VPC in eu-west-1 everything stays in your account.
[04:23] Maya: Great. Another ask from legal - logging retention limits: some regulators require logs for 7 years but others forbid retention of certain categories. Can we configure per-route retention?
[04:34] Priya: Yes - Dedicated and Private allow per-route retention policies and per-customer schemas. Hosted has per-tenant retention tiers but less per-route granularity.
[04:43] Sophie: One more: can Redwood guarantee that no human reviewers see production prompts/responses? Some vendors do red-team review.
[04:50] Alex: We do not use human-in-the-loop logging review on customer production traffic by default. We do have an opt-in program for feedback/troubleshooting where you can opt in to share sample traces with redaction. We'll include that in the security doc.
[05:05] Carlos: Network question: for Private, what are the options - VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or colocated on-prem?
[05:12] Priya: We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for cloud deployments, and we have an on-prem package for air-gapped or highly regulated customers. Each has tradeoffs: peering is straightforward but has maintenance windows; PrivateLink is more controlled for egress; on-prem gives you ultimate isolation but longer provisioning.
[05:29] Ethan: How about latency/cost tradeoffs? If we choose Private in our VPC in EU, what's the typical latency vs hosted?
[05:36] Daniel: Latency is comparable when provisioned nearby; Dedicated/Private can actually reduce variability since you control capacity. Cost per token will be higher for Private since you're paying for reserved infra and networking, and Dedicated sits in the middle. We'll provide a cost model in the follow-up.
[05:52] Maya: Is there support for model pinning and automatic fallbacks? We need predictable outputs for audit.
[05:58] Priya: Yes - you can pin models and we support rollout policies, canaries, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. All audit events for rollouts are captured in the control plane.
[06:08] Sophie: For legal we need to show traceability - who queried what and when. Do you capture request-level audit logs with user and token IDs?
[06:16] Alex: We capture token-level usage metadata; for Dedicated and Private you can correlate tokens to your internal IDs, and we can retain logs as long as you need with proper access controls. We'll provide sample audit log schema.
[06:29] Carlos: One risk is backups / snapshots - do any backups contain unredacted data?
[06:34] Daniel: Backups are encrypted at rest and we can configure snapshot redaction/rotation policies. For Private, backups remain under your account and key control. We'll put the backup handling section in the doc.
[06:48] Maya: Ok, timeline wise - we have a board review mid-December and want a recommendation by then. Possible?
[06:55] Alex: Yes - we'll aim to get security artifacts and a pricing sketch by next week and schedule the infra deep-dive. That should let you prepare a recommendation.
[07:03] Sophie: Is there a POC option to prove residency and log behaviors? We may want a short pilot restricted to EU traffic.
[07:10] Priya: We typically do a scoped pilot on Dedicated or Private. For EU residency proof, spinning up a dedicated small pool in eu-west-1 and routing traffic is the standard approach. We can run sample retention and redaction tests.
[07:22] Ethan: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[07:25] Alex: Biggest blockers are KMS control and legal signoff on DPA. We'll prioritize sending the KMS/HSM integration notes and the DPA + SCCs.
[07:33] Maya: Thank you.
[07:34] Alex: Thanks everyone - quick recap?
[07:36] Alex: Recap: share SOC2/ISO + security whitepaper (Alex), architecture doc for Private + network diag (Priya), customer to send list of sensitive workloads (Carlos), schedule tech deep-dive week of 12/08.
[07:47] Sophie: Sounds good. We'll look out for docs and confirm availability.
[07:51] Alex: Great - we'll follow up in email with links.
[07:55] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps, some product names transcribed as "Redwood wrapped" (should be Redwood Dedicated/Private), minor word swaps.
